Variants.Content: Brand City is the center of the Western Territory of the Marl Bran family, located in the area where hills and mining areas connect. Its name connotes iron, fire and craftsmanship, fitting the reality of the West: Ore must be taken from the ground and passed through miners, furnaces, caravans and merchants before it can become the wealth that can pay debts or arm knights. Wealth also brought tight accounting, oversight by lords and anxiety about road safety. Branded City is not a replica of Casterly Rock, but an intermediate node that turns resources into power.

Entry Ashemark Local families also relied on mining tunnels, pastures, mountain roads, gold and silver circulation and the market sheltered by Casterly Rock; if any road, well or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Ashemark They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the West; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hooves.

Entry Ashemark If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.
Entry Ashemark A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Ashemark They care about the mines, pastures, mountain roads, the circulation of gold and silver, and the market under the protection of Casterly Rock. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see the coat of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
